facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable but must be read as a specialty-finance balance sheet rather than an operating-company credit. The group funds a mortgage, servicing, transitional-lending, asset-management and commercial real estate book mainly with secured repurchase and warehouse lines, secured notes and bonds, and consolidated securitization and fund debt, with a small layer of parent senior unsecured notes. Total contractual debt at September 30, 2026 was US$37,877.221m on the maturity-table basis, of which US$19,680.259m is classed as recourse and US$18,196.962m as non-recourse (10-Q Q3 page:57). The filings report no EBITDA, so the leverage and cover charts carry "Not supplied" and the credit read rests on debt to equity, the recourse split, the maturity profile, unrestricted cash and earnings cover of interest, all derived in Calculations. The strongest contrary evidence to a benign view is the maturity wall: US$7,546.015m falls due October 1 to December 31, 2026 and US$10,619.584m in 2027, and available financing is stated to be uncommitted. Earnings are market-sensitive: the change in fair value of MSRs net of economic hedges was a gain of 121,277 in Q3 2026 against a loss of 264,351 in Q3 2025, and a loss of 475,827 in nine months 2026 against a loss of 752,734 in nine months 2025 (US$ thousands, 10-Q Q3 page:8), and nine-month 2026 net income of 438,665 is below 627,514 in nine months 2025. Earnings available for distribution, a non-GAAP measure, were US$315.3m in Q3 2026 against US$338.9m in Q2 2026 (release Q3 page:1). The senior unsecured notes are unsecured and, at issuance, not guaranteed by any subsidiary, so they rank behind secured lenders on pledged collateral and behind subsidiary-level debt in the structure (10-Q Q3 page:59). The strongest supportive evidence is the filed statement that Rithm was in compliance with all debt covenants at September 30, 2026 and that about US$1.1 billion of liquidity held in the servicers exceeds regulatory requirements. Neither can be tested further without the facility agreements and indentures.

facts.text: 1. Total debt, refining the CP-0 entry. CP-0 listed the MD&A total of "$38.1 billion", the Note 17 face total and the maturity-table total as three unreconciled figures. The first two can now be bridged: the maturity-table total of US$37,877.221m equals the Note 17 face total of US$36,102.221m plus the US$1,775.000m principal of the three senior notes (calculation below); the same bridge holds at December 31, 2025 (US$34,168.392m plus US$1,275.000m equals US$35,443.392m). The MD&A figure of US$38.1 billion remains unreconciled: it is US$222.779m above the maturity-table total, more than rounding to one decimal of a billion can explain. This module uses the maturity-table total for maturities and recourse split, and the Note 17 carrying total plus senior notes for carrying debt, and names the basis each time. 2. Cash scopes, as CP-0 recorded. Cash and cash equivalents US$1,708.750m; plus restricted cash US$740.572m and restricted cash of consolidated entities US$101.715m gives US$2,551.037m, the cash flow statement total (10-Q Q3 page:44), while the balance sheet line "Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash" of US$2,449.322m excludes the restricted cash of consolidated entities (10-Q Q3 page:7, page:44). This reconciles US$2,551.037m to US$2,449.322m by US$101.715m (calculation below). 3. Senior notes issuance proceeds, as CP-0 recorded. The nine-month 2026 cash flow line "Proceeds from issuance of unsecured senior notes" is 495,000 in both 2026 and 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:13), while the 2031 notes of May 14, 2026 raised approximately US$493.7 million net (10-Q Q3 page:58) and the only other issue, the 2030 notes of June 20, 2025, raised approximately US$495.0 million (10-K page:315). The 2026 line is not explained in the retained text. Note 17 amounts control for the notes. 4. Presentation change. The FY2025 income statement shows interest, general and administrative, and compensation as the only expense lines, with depreciation and amortization of 107,477 inside general and administrative (10-K page:199); the 10-Q presents it as a separate line and reclassifies prior periods (10-Q Q3 page:17, page:8). The new commercial real estate segment contributes revenue of US$547,428 thousand in nine months 2026 and none in nine months 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:8), so nine-month 2026 against 2025 is not like-for-like. 5. Release comparatives. The Q3 release compares the balance sheet with June 30, 2026, the 10-Q with December 31, 2025. Figures here are taken from the 10-Q.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Debt bridge, face to maturity table. Sep 30, 2026: 36,102,221 (Note 17 total face, page:54) + 775,000 + 500,000 + 500,000 (senior notes principal, page:168) = 37,877,221, equal to the maturity-table total (page:57). Dec 31, 2025: 34,168,392 (10-K page:311) + 775,000 + 500,000 = 35,443,392, equal to the maturity-table total (10-K page:314). The MD&A figure: 38,100,000 less 37,877,221 = 222,779 (using the printed US$38.1 billion). 2. Carrying total of Note 17: 14,235,647 + 14,011,438 + 7,399,680 = 35,646,765, equal to the printed total (page:54). Including senior notes, net: 35,646,765 + 1,755,476 = 37,402,241 (Sep 30, 2026); 33,865,374 + 1,258,271 = 35,123,645 (Dec 31, 2025). Net of unrestricted cash for Sep 30, 2026: 37,402,241 - 1,708,750 = 35,693,491 (arithmetic only; not a leverage metric because no EBITDA exists). 3. Recourse share of maturity-table debt at Sep 30, 2026: 19,680,259 / 37,877,221 = 0.5196 (51.96%); non-recourse 18,196,962 / 37,877,221 = 0.4804. Dec 31, 2025 recourse: 19,496,781 / 35,443,392 = 0.5501. 4. Near-term maturities: Oct 1 to Dec 31, 2026 and 2027 together = 7,546,015 + 10,619,584 = 18,165,599 (a 15-month window to December 31, 2027, not twelve months), of which recourse 6,230,073 + 6,736,955 = 12,967,028. Share of total: 18,165,599 / 37,877,221 = 0.4796; recourse share of the window: 12,967,028 / 18,165,599 = 0.7138. Unrestricted cash 1,708,750 against the Q4 2026 recourse bucket of 6,230,073: 0.2743. 5. Available financing check: 3,021,445 + 3,918,467 + 459,656 + 148,000 + 402,000 + 2,704,263 + 59,722 + 71,731 = 10,785,284, equal to the printed total (page:57); capacity 29,121,824 less outstanding 18,336,540 = 10,785,284. 6. Debt to equity (principal basis, equity in Rithm Capital Corp. including preferred stock): Sep 30, 2026: 37,877,221 / 8,620,062 = 4.394x (4.39x); Dec 31, 2025: 35,443,392 / 8,430,487 = 4.204x (4.20x). Recourse: 19,680,259 / 8,620,062 = 2.283x (2.28x); 19,496,781 / 8,430,487 = 2.313x (2.31x). The recourse column includes secured repurchase and warehouse borrowings made by the Company against collateral, not only unsecured debt, and equity includes the preferred stock carrying value of 1,632,915 (Sep 30, 2026) and 1,390,790 (Dec 31, 2025); neither ratio is a covenant measure. 7. Earnings cover of interest, (pre-tax income + interest expense and warehouse line fees) / interest expense and warehouse line fees: FY2025 (806,383 + 1,662,433) / 1,662,433 = 1.485x; nine months 2025 (600,058 + 1,239,612) / 1,239,612 = 1.484x; nine months 2026 (760,219 + 1,395,011) / 1,395,011 = 1.545x. Pre-tax income includes MSR fair value changes and other non-cash items, and interest on warehouse funding is a cost of revenue for this issuer, so this is a rough indicator, not EBITDA cover and not a cash measure. Cash paid for interest and warehouse line fees for nine months 2026 was 1,406,118 against expense of 1,395,011, a difference of 11,107. 8. Cash scope reconciliation (10-Q Q3 page:44): 1,708,750 + 740,572 + 101,715 = 2,551,037; 2,551,037 - 101,715 = 2,449,322, the balance sheet line (page:7). The US$1.7 billion MD&A figure matches 1,708,750 rounded. 9. Unit conversion for the chart tables: thousands divided by 1,000, for example 7,546,015 gives 7,546.015 US$m. 10. Not computed: net debt to EBITDA, EBITDA cover and any committed liquidity figure, because the numerators are not supplied (see Gaps). No LTM figure is used in any table.

rows.label: Rithm is a large, mostly secured and heavily short-dated funder of mortgage and real estate assets. Debt is about half recourse, near-term maturities are heavy, unrestricted cash is modest against them, and no EBITDA is reported.
Contractual maturities through the end of 2027 are a large share of total debt, with a big part recourse to the parent.
Available financing under secured lines is described as uncommitted and collateral-dependent.
Leverage on equity is high on a total basis and meaningfully lower on a recourse basis.
Earnings are volatile because of mortgage servicing rights fair value changes, and nine-month 2026 earnings are below the prior year.
The filings print compliance statements but no covenant levels or headroom.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Rithm Capital Corp. is a publicly listed, internally managed REIT that describes itself as a global asset manager focused on real estate, credit and financial services (10-K page:8). It is not a sponsor-owned credit; the pack names no controlling shareholder and the Part III ownership information is incorporated by reference from a proxy statement that is not in the pack (10-K page:3). The operating model is an integrated platform of five reported segments: Origination and Servicing (Newrez and NRM), Residential Transitional Lending (Genesis), Asset Management (Sculptor, Crestline and Rithm Advisers), Investment Portfolio and Commercial Real Estate (Elecor) (10-Q Q3 page:14 to page:16). Origination and Servicing is the largest business by assets, equity and earnings contribution (10-Q Q3 page:132); in the nine months to September 30, 2026 it produced US$968,563 thousand of segment pre-tax income against group pre-tax income of US$760,219 thousand, so the other segments and the corporate category net to a loss (10-Q Q3 page:25). The credit mechanic is that revenue in the largest segment depends on the fair value of mortgage servicing rights and on origination margins, both rate-sensitive, while funding is mostly secured and short-dated (CP-1). The December 2025 acquisitions of Crestline (cash consideration US$324.7 million, bringing insurance and reinsurance strategies and interest-sensitive insurance contract liabilities) and Paramount, now Elecor (total consideration approximately US$1.8 billion, 12.2 million square feet of Class A offices in New York City and San Francisco) are the main credit-relevant change in history (10-Q Q3 page:20; page:150). They bring fixed operating costs, depreciation and property debt: depreciation and amortization rose to US$278,619 thousand in nine months 2026 from US$71,492 thousand (10-Q Q3 page:8). Asset Management and Commercial Real Estate both reported pre-tax losses in the nine months (10-Q Q3 page:25). No leveraged buyout, sponsor recapitalisation, priming, uptiering or collateral release is documented in the pack. The financing actions documented are plain senior unsecured note issues, a preferred equity issue and securitizations, set out in the transaction summary below. What cannot be assessed is legal capacity under the notes, because the indentures are not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On May 14, 2026 Rithm Capital Corp. issued US$500.0 million of 8.500% senior unsecured notes due June 1, 2031 in a private offering, for net proceeds of approximately US$493.7 million, under an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association; interest is payable on June 1 and December 1 from December 1, 2026; the notes are redeemable from June 1, 2028 at 104.250 stepping to 100.000 from 2030, and before then at a make-whole price or up to 40% at 108.500 with equity proceeds; they rank equally with the Company's other senior unsecured debt and were not guaranteed by any subsidiary at issuance (10-Q Q3 page:58 to page:59). The 10-Q does not state the use of proceeds in the text read; the nine-month cash flow statement shows repayment of unsecured notes of US$18,326 thousand and no large unsecured repayment, so the issue increased unsecured debt (10-Q Q3 page:13). Status: closed and outstanding. Liquidity effect: adds to cash and extends the unsecured profile to 2031; it also adds interest cost at 8.500%. Earlier senior notes: US$500.0 million of 8.000% notes due July 15, 2030 issued June 20, 2025, and US$775.0 million of 8.000% notes due April 1, 2029 issued March 19, 2024 (10-Q Q3 page:168); the notes due October 15, 2025 were redeemed in the second quarter of 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:63). The three outstanding notes each carry a requirement that Total Unencumbered Assets be not less than 120% of outstanding unsecured debt, and the 2029 and 2030 notes carry a 101% repurchase right on a change of control or Mortgage Business Triggering Event (10-Q Q3 page:61; page:63; page:168).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Origination and Servicing earned the large majority of nine-month 2026 segment pre-tax income, and change in fair value of MSRs net of economic hedges was a gain in Q3 2026 and a loss in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:8; page:25). Mechanic: servicing and origination revenue depends on interest rate and prepayment moves and origination volume, so reported income can swing without a change in cash earnings. Implication: coverage of funding costs is less predictable than for a fee-based or contract-based issuer; committee should look at cash servicing fees separately from fair value changes. A logged conflict that counters this: none. A limitation that counters it: the nine months include acquisition effects. 2. Business mix shift. Evidence: Asset Management and Commercial Real Estate reported pre-tax losses in nine months 2026 while depreciation and amortization rose (10-Q Q3 page:8; page:25). Mechanic: acquired real estate and an asset manager add fixed costs, interest expense on property debt and depreciation before fee or rent growth scales. Implication: near-term earnings support for debt service from the new businesses is unproven; progress depends on leasing (occupancy 83.5% against 85.3% at December 31, 2025, recalculated for the joint venture sale, 10-Q Q3 page:150) and AUM inflows (management language, release Q3 page:1 to page:2). 3. Structural position. Evidence: the senior notes are unsecured and were not guaranteed by any subsidiary at issuance, while much of the debt is secured or sits in consolidated non-recourse entities (10-Q Q3 page:56; page:59; CP-1). Mechanic: parent noteholders have claims on parent assets and distributions from subsidiaries after subsidiary creditors. Implication: loss given default for the notes depends on residual value after secured and subsidiary creditors; no recovery conclusion is given here. 4. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor; internally managed; insiders invest alongside clients (10-Q Q3 page:121). Mechanic: the owner base is public shareholders and management, so there is no sponsor extraction channel documented, but dividends are required for REIT status. Implication: neutral on documented actions; ownership concentration is Insufficient Information. 5. Key uncertainties: legal capacity under the notes, the composition of the Paramount consideration, and ratings, all missing from the pack.

Mechanic: servicing and origination revenue depends on interest rate and prepayment moves and origination volume, so reported income can swing without a change in cash earnings. Implication: coverage of funding costs is less predictable than for a fee-based or contract-based issuer; committee should look at cash servicing fees separately from fair value changes. A logged conflict that counters this: none. A limitation that counters it: the nine months include acquisition effects.

2. Business mix shift. Evidence: Asset Management and Commercial Real Estate reported pre-tax losses in nine months 2026 while depreciation and amortization rose (10-Q Q3 page:8; page:25). Mechanic: acquired real estate and an asset manager add fixed costs, interest expense on property debt and depreciation before fee or rent growth scales. Implication: near-term earnings support for debt service from the new businesses is unproven; progress depends on leasing (occupancy 83.5% against 85.3% at December 31, 2025, recalculated for the joint venture sale, 10-Q Q3 page:150) and AUM inflows (management language, release Q3 page:1 to page:2).

3. Structural position. Evidence: the senior notes are unsecured and were not guaranteed by any subsidiary at issuance, while much of the debt is secured or sits in consolidated non-recourse entities (10-Q Q3 page:56; page:59; CP-1). Mechanic: parent noteholders have claims on parent assets and distributions from subsidiaries after subsidiary creditors. Implication: loss given default for the notes depends on residual value after secured and subsidiary creditors; no recovery conclusion is given here.

4. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor; internally managed; insiders invest alongside clients (10-Q Q3 page:121). Mechanic: the owner base is public shareholders and management, so there is no sponsor extraction channel documented, but dividends are required for REIT status. Implication: neutral on documented actions; ownership concentration is Insufficient Information.
5. Key uncertainties: legal capacity under the notes, the composition of the Paramount consideration, and ratings, all missing from the pack.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Rithm Capital Corp. is a large, diversified mortgage and real estate finance platform whose credit quality rests on refinancing short-dated, mostly secured funding rather than on stable cash earnings, and the fundamental view is neutral to cautious with medium confidence. The strongest support is a dominant, profitable Origination and Servicing segment, a stated position of compliance with all debt covenants, USD 1,708.750 million of unrestricted cash and repeated senior unsecured note issuance in 2024, 2025 and 2026. The weakest point is the maturity profile: USD 7,546.015 million falls due in Q4 2026 and USD 10,619.584 million in 2027, about half of contractual debt is recourse, and available financing is described as uncommitted. Continued access to secured funding, stable servicing values and the new real estate and asset management businesses reaching profit will decide the outcome.
facts.basis: Literal wrapped paragraph from the model-authored handoff; no new analysis.

The strongest support is a dominant, profitable Origination and Servicing segment, a stated position of compliance with all debt covenants, USD 1,708.750 million of unrestricted cash and repeated senior unsecured note issuance in 2024, 2025 and 2026. The weakest point is the maturity profile: USD 7,546.015 million falls due in Q4 2026 and USD 10,619.584 million in 2027, about half of contractual debt is recourse, and available financing is described as uncommitted. Continued access to secured funding, stable servicing values and the new real estate and asset management businesses reaching profit will decide the outcome.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the maturity profile is the central risk. Contractual debt at September 30, 2026 was USD 37,877.221 million on the maturity-table basis, of which USD 19,680.259 million is recourse and USD 18,196.962 million non-recourse [CP-1, chart data and calculations]. Maturities of USD 7,546.015 million in the fourth quarter of 2026 and USD 10,619.584 million in 2027 together are USD 18,165.599 million, a 15-month window holding 47.96% of the total, and USD 12,967.028 million of that window is recourse [CP-1, calculations 4]. Mechanically, most of these are secured warehouse, repurchase and servicing lines that Rithm rolls routinely, so default risk turns on lender willingness and collateral values rather than on cash generation. The implication for creditors is that a pause in secured funding markets or a fall in collateral values would force asset sales or margin posting into a thin cash cushion.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, liquidity is thinner than the capacity figure suggests. Unrestricted cash was USD 1,708.750 million at September 30, 2026, against USD 1,847.626 million at December 31, 2025, and 27.43% of the USD 6,230.073 million recourse maturity of the fourth quarter of 2026 [CP-1, liquidity and calculations]. Available financing of USD 10,785.284 million is stated to be uncommitted and collateral-dependent, so none of it is counted as undrawn committed liquidity. Management expects cash, operating cash flow and the ability to extend or refinance secured lines to cover needs for twelve months, and says its ability to extend or refinance short-term borrowings is critical to its outlook [CP-1, liquidity]. The implication is that headroom cannot be measured from the pack, and margin calls on USD 14.2 billion of secured financing agreements would draw on the same cash.

Demonstrated market access: the 8.500% notes due 2031 were issued on May 14, 2026 for net proceeds of about USD 493.7 million, a Series F preferred raised about USD 242.1 million in January 2026, and management reports several securitizations in Q3 2026, which is Management Language [CP-1A, transaction summary]. Stated compliance: the filings say Rithm was in compliance with all debt covenants and that about USD 1.1 billion of liquidity at the servicers exceeds regulatory requirements, Documentary Fact but unverifiable without the agreements [CP-1, liquidity and covenants]. Transparency: quarterly reporting, an unqualified FY2025 audit and effective disclosure controls support monitoring, Documentary Fact [CP-1A, governance table].

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The supplied annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases are enough to start the requested snapshot work for Rithm Capital Corp., with bounded limits. No downstream step is blocked on sources. | Medium | No indentures, credit agreements, ratings or presentation decks were supplied, so debt terms rest on filing summaries only. |

### Readiness view

The effective source set is adequate for the requested snapshot work, with limitations. The four periodic reports and three earnings releases are filed or furnished issuer documents with located financial statements, debt, liquidity, covenant, segment and subsequent-event disclosure, and the latest period (Q3 2026) is covered by both a quarterly report and a release. The view for each consumer is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. The strongest limiting evidence is that the covenant and guarantee terms of the senior unsecured notes are known only through the 10-Q summaries, because the indentures themselves are not in the pack, and that no external rating, quote or market data exists in the pack or the context. Nothing found makes a consumer CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. This is a statement about source sufficiency only; it does not say any downstream analysis is complete or that any model input contract is met.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Rithm is a large, mostly secured and heavily short-dated funder of mortgage and real estate assets. Debt is about half recourse, near-term maturities are heavy, unrestricted cash is modest against them, and no EBITDA is reported. | Medium | Committed undrawn capacity, covenant levels and the unencumbered-asset figure are not printed, so liquidity headroom and covenant headroom cannot be calculated. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Contractual maturities through the end of 2027 are a large share of total debt, with a big part recourse to the parent. | Refinancing and rollover of secured lines is the central credit risk for parent creditors. | High |

| Available financing under secured lines is described as uncommitted and collateral-dependent. | Stated capacity is not committed liquidity, so true headroom is lower than the capacity figure suggests. | High |
| Leverage on equity is high on a total basis and meaningfully lower on a recourse basis. | The senior unsecured notes sit behind secured and structurally senior non-recourse debt. | Medium |

| Earnings are volatile because of mortgage servicing rights fair value changes, and nine-month 2026 earnings are below the prior year. | Coverage of funding costs depends on market-sensitive items, not stable cash earnings. | Medium |
| The filings print compliance statements but no covenant levels or headroom. | Covenant risk cannot be measured from the pack; only compliance is evidenced. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is usable but must be read as a specialty-finance balance sheet rather than an operating-company credit. The group funds a mortgage, servicing, transitional-lending, asset-management and commercial real estate book mainly with secured repurchase and warehouse lines, secured notes and bonds, and consolidated securitization and fund debt, with a small layer of parent senior unsecured notes. Total contractual debt at September 30, 2026 was US$37,877.221m on the maturity-table basis, of which US$19,680.259m is classed as recourse and US$18,196.962m as non-recourse (10-Q Q3 page:57). The filings report no EBITDA, so the leverage and cover charts carry "Not supplied" and the credit read rests on debt to equity, the recourse split, the maturity profile, unrestricted cash and earnings cover of interest, all derived in Calculations. The strongest contrary evidence to a benign view is the maturity wall: US$7,546.015m falls due October 1 to December 31, 2026 and US$10,619.584m in 2027, and available financing is stated to be uncommitted. Earnings are market-sensitive: the change in fair value of MSRs net of economic hedges was a gain of 121,277 in Q3 2026 against a loss of 264,351 in Q3 2025, and a loss of 475,827 in nine months 2026 against a loss of 752,734 in nine months 2025 (US$ thousands, 10-Q Q3 page:8), and nine-month 2026 net income of 438,665 is below 627,514 in nine months 2025. Earnings available for distribution, a non-GAAP measure, were US$315.3m in Q3 2026 against US$338.9m in Q2 2026 (release Q3 page:1). The senior unsecured notes are unsecured and, at issuance, not guaranteed by any subsidiary, so they rank behind secured lenders on pledged collateral and behind subsidiary-level debt in the structure (10-Q Q3 page:59). The strongest supportive evidence is the filed statement that Rithm was in compliance with all debt covenants at September 30, 2026 and that about US$1.1 billion of liquidity held in the servicers exceeds regulatory requirements. Neither can be tested further without the facility agreements and indentures.

### Conflicts, corrections and carried-forward limitations

1. Total debt, refining the CP-0 entry. CP-0 listed the MD&A total of "$38.1 billion", the Note 17 face total and the maturity-table total as three unreconciled figures. The first two can now be bridged: the maturity-table total of US$37,877.221m equals the Note 17 face total of US$36,102.221m plus the US$1,775.000m principal of the three senior notes (calculation below); the same bridge holds at December 31, 2025 (US$34,168.392m plus US$1,275.000m equals US$35,443.392m). The MD&A figure of US$38.1 billion remains unreconciled: it is US$222.779m above the maturity-table total, more than rounding to one decimal of a billion can explain. This module uses the maturity-table total for maturities and recourse split, and the Note 17 carrying total plus senior notes for carrying debt, and names the basis each time.

2. Cash scopes, as CP-0 recorded. Cash and cash equivalents US$1,708.750m; plus restricted cash US$740.572m and restricted cash of consolidated entities US$101.715m gives US$2,551.037m, the cash flow statement total (10-Q Q3 page:44), while the balance sheet line "Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash" of US$2,449.322m excludes the restricted cash of consolidated entities (10-Q Q3 page:7, page:44). This reconciles US$2,551.037m to US$2,449.322m by US$101.715m (calculation below).

3. Senior notes issuance proceeds, as CP-0 recorded. The nine-month 2026 cash flow line "Proceeds from issuance of unsecured senior notes" is 495,000 in both 2026 and 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:13), while the 2031 notes of May 14, 2026 raised approximately US$493.7 million net (10-Q Q3 page:58) and the only other issue, the 2030 notes of June 20, 2025, raised approximately US$495.0 million (10-K page:315). The 2026 line is not explained in the retained text. Note 17 amounts control for the notes.

4. Presentation change. The FY2025 income statement shows interest, general and administrative, and compensation as the only expense lines, with depreciation and amortization of 107,477 inside general and administrative (10-K page:199); the 10-Q presents it as a separate line and reclassifies prior periods (10-Q Q3 page:17, page:8). The new commercial real estate segment contributes revenue of US$547,428 thousand in nine months 2026 and none in nine months 2025 (10-Q Q3 page:8), so nine-month 2026 against 2025 is not like-for-like.
5. Release comparatives. The Q3 release compares the balance sheet with June 30, 2026, the 10-Q with December 31, 2025. Figures here are taken from the 10-Q.
## Calculations
All inputs are in US$ thousands unless stated. Locators are those listed above.

1. Debt bridge, face to maturity table. Sep 30, 2026: 36,102,221 (Note 17 total face, page:54) + 775,000 + 500,000 + 500,000 (senior notes principal, page:168) = 37,877,221, equal to the maturity-table total (page:57). Dec 31, 2025: 34,168,392 (10-K page:311) + 775,000 + 500,000 = 35,443,392, equal to the maturity-table total (10-K page:314). The MD&A figure: 38,100,000 less 37,877,221 = 222,779 (using the printed US$38.1 billion).

2. Carrying total of Note 17: 14,235,647 + 14,011,438 + 7,399,680 = 35,646,765, equal to the printed total (page:54). Including senior notes, net: 35,646,765 + 1,755,476 = 37,402,241 (Sep 30, 2026); 33,865,374 + 1,258,271 = 35,123,645 (Dec 31, 2025). Net of unrestricted cash for Sep 30, 2026: 37,402,241 - 1,708,750 = 35,693,491 (arithmetic only; not a leverage metric because no EBITDA exists).

4. Near-term maturities: Oct 1 to Dec 31, 2026 and 2027 together = 7,546,015 + 10,619,584 = 18,165,599 (a 15-month window to December 31, 2027, not twelve months), of which recourse 6,230,073 + 6,736,955 = 12,967,028. Share of total: 18,165,599 / 37,877,221 = 0.4796; recourse share of the window: 12,967,028 / 18,165,599 = 0.7138. Unrestricted cash 1,708,750 against the Q4 2026 recourse bucket of 6,230,073: 0.2743.

6. Debt to equity (principal basis, equity in Rithm Capital Corp. including preferred stock): Sep 30, 2026: 37,877,221 / 8,620,062 = 4.394x (4.39x); Dec 31, 2025: 35,443,392 / 8,430,487 = 4.204x (4.20x). Recourse: 19,680,259 / 8,620,062 = 2.283x (2.28x); 19,496,781 / 8,430,487 = 2.313x (2.31x). The recourse column includes secured repurchase and warehouse borrowings made by the Company against collateral, not only unsecured debt, and equity includes the preferred stock carrying value of 1,632,915 (Sep 30, 2026) and 1,390,790 (Dec 31, 2025); neither ratio is a covenant measure.

7. Earnings cover of interest, (pre-tax income + interest expense and warehouse line fees) / interest expense and warehouse line fees: FY2025 (806,383 + 1,662,433) / 1,662,433 = 1.485x; nine months 2025 (600,058 + 1,239,612) / 1,239,612 = 1.484x; nine months 2026 (760,219 + 1,395,011) / 1,395,011 = 1.545x. Pre-tax income includes MSR fair value changes and other non-cash items, and interest on warehouse funding is a cost of revenue for this issuer, so this is a rough indicator, not EBITDA cover and not a cash measure. Cash paid for interest and warehouse line fees for nine months 2026 was 1,406,118 against expense of 1,395,011, a difference of 11,107.

8. Cash scope reconciliation (10-Q Q3 page:44): 1,708,750 + 740,572 + 101,715 = 2,551,037; 2,551,037 - 101,715 = 2,449,322, the balance sheet line (page:7). The US$1.7 billion MD&A figure matches 1,708,750 rounded.
9. Unit conversion for the chart tables: thousands divided by 1,000, for example 7,546,015 gives 7,546.015 US$m.
10. Not computed: net debt to EBITDA, EBITDA cover and any committed liquidity figure, because the numerators are not supplied (see Gaps). No LTM figure is used in any table.

## Next module

Proceed to CP-1A with these financial facts: a group with a mostly secured and short-dated funding stack where about half of contractual debt is recourse, a recourse maturity wall in the next five quarters, uncommitted lines and no EBITDA metric. CP-1A should explain the business and acquisition changes (Crestline in December 2025, Elecor, the new commercial real estate and asset management segments, the wind-down of the single-family rental business referred to in the 10-Q) that drive the figures, and should carry forward the conflicts and gaps listed above, in particular the unreconciled total-debt figures, the absent EBITDA and covenant levels, and the non-like-for-like nine-month comparison.

### Reader summary

Two large acquisitions in December 2025 changed its mix toward real estate ownership and asset management, which are not yet profitable. | Medium | No proxy statement, indentures or investor decks were supplied, so ownership, creditor-protection terms and management plans are not verified. |

### Business and transaction view

Rithm Capital Corp. is a publicly listed, internally managed REIT that describes itself as a global asset manager focused on real estate, credit and financial services (10-K page:8). It is not a sponsor-owned credit; the pack names no controlling shareholder and the Part III ownership information is incorporated by reference from a proxy statement that is not in the pack (10-K page:3). The operating model is an integrated platform of five reported segments: Origination and Servicing (Newrez and NRM), Residential Transitional Lending (Genesis), Asset Management (Sculptor, Crestline and Rithm Advisers), Investment Portfolio and Commercial Real Estate (Elecor) (10-Q Q3 page:14 to page:16). Origination and Servicing is the largest business by assets, equity and earnings contribution (10-Q Q3 page:132); in the nine months to September 30, 2026 it produced US$968,563 thousand of segment pre-tax income against group pre-tax income of US$760,219 thousand, so the other segments and the corporate category net to a loss (10-Q Q3 page:25). The credit mechanic is that revenue in the largest segment depends on the fair value of mortgage servicing rights and on origination margins, both rate-sensitive, while funding is mostly secured and short-dated (CP-1). The December 2025 acquisitions of Crestline (cash consideration US$324.7 million, bringing insurance and reinsurance strategies and interest-sensitive insurance contract liabilities) and Paramount, now Elecor (total consideration approximately US$1.8 billion, 12.2 million square feet of Class A offices in New York City and San Francisco) are the main credit-relevant change in history (10-Q Q3 page:20; page:150). They bring fixed operating costs, depreciation and property debt: depreciation and amortization rose to US$278,619 thousand in nine months 2026 from US$71,492 thousand (10-Q Q3 page:8). Asset Management and Commercial Real Estate both reported pre-tax losses in the nine months (10-Q Q3 page:25). No leveraged buyout, sponsor recapitalisation, priming, uptiering or collateral release is documented in the pack. The financing actions documented are plain senior unsecured note issues, a preferred equity issue and securitizations, set out in the transaction summary below. What cannot be assessed is legal capacity under the notes, because the indentures are not supplied.

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Origination and Servicing earned the large majority of nine-month 2026 segment pre-tax income, and change in fair value of MSRs net of economic hedges was a gain in Q3 2026 and a loss in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:8; page:25). Implication: coverage of funding costs is less predictable than for a fee-based or contract-based issuer; committee should look at cash servicing fees separately from fair value changes. A logged conflict that counters this: none. A limitation that counters it: the nine months include acquisition effects.

2. Business mix shift. Evidence: Asset Management and Commercial Real Estate reported pre-tax losses in nine months 2026 while depreciation and amortization rose (10-Q Q3 page:8; page:25). The CP-1 conflicts on total debt, cash scope and senior note proceeds are inherited and unchanged.
### Consumer notes

CP-2 should take from this module: the segment profit concentration, the loss-making new segments, the structural position of the notes and the governance read as neutral on documented actions. Segment equity in Rithm Capital Corp. 5,405,211 + 1,019,643 + 1,278,905 + 1,632,030 + 1,128,787 + (1,844,514) = 8,620,062, equal to the balance sheet (10-Q Q3 page:7). ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Neutral to cautious. A profitable mortgage servicing and origination core and demonstrated market access support the credit, but heavy near-term maturities, uncommitted funding lines and a structurally junior position for the unsecured notes dominate. | Medium | No indentures, committed-liquidity data, covenant levels or ratings were supplied, and no EBITDA is reported. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |
| Debt due in the fourth quarter of 2026 and in 2027 is a large share of total debt, with a big recourse part. | Refinancing success is the main driver of default risk for parent creditors. | High |

| Available secured financing is uncommitted and tied to collateral, while unrestricted cash is small against the nearest recourse maturities. | Liquidity depends on lenders rolling lines, so a market shock could cut capacity quickly. | High |

| The senior notes are unsecured and not guaranteed by subsidiaries, while about half of debt is recourse and much of the rest is secured or non-recourse. | Noteholders rank behind collateralised lenders and subsidiary creditors, which weighs on loss given default. | Medium |

| Earnings are rate-sensitive, nine-month 2026 net income fell, and the two newest segments lost money before tax. | Cover of funding costs is modest and less predictable than cash-based earnings. | Medium |
### Credit view

Rithm Capital Corp. is a large, diversified mortgage and real estate finance platform whose credit quality rests on refinancing short-dated, mostly secured funding rather than on stable cash earnings, and the fundamental view is neutral to cautious with medium confidence. The strongest support is a dominant, profitable Origination and Servicing segment, a stated position of compliance with all debt covenants, USD 1,708.750 million of unrestricted cash and repeated senior unsecured note issuance in 2024, 2025 and 2026. The weakest point is the maturity profile: USD 7,546.015 million falls due in Q4 2026 and USD 10,619.584 million in 2027, about half of contractual debt is recourse, and available financing is described as uncommitted. Continued access to secured funding, stable servicing values and the new real estate and asset management businesses reaching profit will decide the outcome.
### Key findings

First, the maturity profile is the central risk. Contractual debt at September 30, 2026 was USD 37,877.221 million on the maturity-table basis, of which USD 19,680.259 million is recourse and USD 18,196.962 million non-recourse [CP-1, chart data and calculations]. Maturities of USD 7,546.015 million in the fourth quarter of 2026 and USD 10,619.584 million in 2027 together are USD 18,165.599 million, a 15-month window holding 47.96% of the total, and USD 12,967.028 million of that window is recourse [CP-1, calculations 4]. Mechanically, most of these are secured warehouse, repurchase and servicing lines that Rithm rolls routinely, so default risk turns on lender willingness and collateral values rather than on cash generation. The implication for creditors is that a pause in secured funding markets or a fall in collateral values would force asset sales or margin posting into a thin cash cushion.

Second, liquidity is thinner than the capacity figure suggests. Unrestricted cash was USD 1,708.750 million at September 30, 2026, against USD 1,847.626 million at December 31, 2025, and 27.43% of the USD 6,230.073 million recourse maturity of the fourth quarter of 2026 [CP-1, liquidity and calculations]. Available financing of USD 10,785.284 million is stated to be uncommitted and collateral-dependent, so none of it is counted as undrawn committed liquidity. Management expects cash, operating cash flow and the ability to extend or refinance secured lines to cover needs for twelve months, and says its ability to extend or refinance short-term borrowings is critical to its outlook [CP-1, liquidity]. The implication is that headroom cannot be measured from the pack, and margin calls on USD 14.2 billion of secured financing agreements would draw on the same cash.

Third, leverage is high on a total basis and lower on a recourse basis. Principal-basis debt to equity in Rithm Capital Corp. was 4.39x at September 30, 2026 against 4.20x at December 31, 2025, and recourse debt to equity was 2.28x against 2.31x [CP-1, calculations 6]. Neither is a covenant measure and recourse debt includes collateralised repurchase and warehouse borrowings. No EBITDA is reported, so conventional leverage and cover ratios are not supplied.

Fourth, earnings quality is weak relative to the funding stack. Pre-tax income plus interest expense over interest expense was 1.54x for nine months 2026, 1.48x for nine months 2025 and 1.49x for FY2025, and includes fair value changes on mortgage servicing rights; the change in fair value of MSRs net of hedges was a gain in Q3 2026 and a loss in nine months 2026 [CP-1, calculations 7; CP-1, base view]. Net income for nine months 2026 was USD 438.665 million against USD 627.514 million, income tax expense was USD 321.554 million against a benefit of USD 27.456 million while cash taxes were USD 11.398 million, so the tax charge appears to be largely non-cash, Analyst Interpretation [CP-1, financials table]. Origination and Servicing produced USD 968.563 million of segment pre-tax income in nine months 2026, against group pre-tax income of USD 760.219 million, so the other segments and corporate costs net to a loss [CP-1A, company and operating model]. Asset Management reported a pre-tax loss of USD 83.484 million and Commercial Real Estate a loss of USD 74.855 million.

Fifth, the notes sit behind other claims. The three senior unsecured notes, USD 775.000 million at 8.000% due 2029, USD 500.000 million at 8.000% due 2030 and USD 500.000 million at 8.500% due 2031, are unsecured, were not guaranteed by any subsidiary at issuance, and require Total Unencumbered Assets of at least 120% of unsecured debt [CP-1, debt instruments; CP-1A, transaction summary]. Collateral of consolidated securitization entities is not available to other creditors of the parent. Total Unencumbered Assets is not printed, so headroom on the 120% test cannot be calculated. As a recovery mechanic only, residual value for noteholders is what remains after secured and subsidiary creditors, and no recovery outcome is concluded here.

Sixth, governance on documented actions is neutral. No sponsor or controlling holder is identified, the REIT distribution rule requires regular payouts, a Series F preferred was issued in January 2026, and no priming, uptiering or collateral release is documented, but legal capacity under the indentures cannot be assessed because they were not supplied [CP-1A, governance table].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Scale and diversification: nine-month 2026 revenue of USD 4,423.413 million came from five segments, with Origination and Servicing the largest by assets, equity and earnings, and the servicing portfolio of about USD 878.9 billion of unpaid principal balance is a recurring-fee base [CP-1A, company profile; Documentary Fact]. Demonstrated market access: the 8.500% notes due 2031 were issued on May 14, 2026 for net proceeds of about USD 493.7 million, a Series F preferred raised about USD 242.1 million in January 2026, and management reports several securitizations in Q3 2026, which is Management Language [CP-1A, transaction summary]. Stated compliance: the filings say Rithm was in compliance with all debt covenants and that about USD 1.1 billion of liquidity at the servicers exceeds regulatory requirements, Documentary Fact but unverifiable without the agreements [CP-1, liquidity and covenants]. Lower recourse leverage than total leverage: recourse debt to equity of 2.28x is about half the total ratio of 4.39x, Analyst Interpretation of the CP-1 ratios. Transparency: quarterly reporting, an unqualified FY2025 audit and effective disclosure controls support monitoring, Documentary Fact [CP-1A, governance table].

Weaknesses. Refinancing concentration: USD 18,165.599 million of debt falls due within the 15 months to December 31, 2027, Documentary Fact and derived [CP-1]. Uncommitted funding: available financing is uncommitted and collateral-dependent, Documentary Fact. Earnings sensitivity and negative operating cash flow: operating cash flow for nine months 2026 was an outflow of USD 1,313.851 million because loans originated for sale are in operating cash flow, offset by financing inflows of USD 3,597.283 million; this is Documentary Fact and the reading that the group depends on continuous external funding is Analyst Interpretation [CP-1, financials table]. Structural subordination of the unsecured notes, Analyst Interpretation of the guarantee and recourse facts. Loss-making new segments after the December 2025 acquisitions of Crestline and Paramount (now Elecor), whose depreciation and amortization of USD 278.619 million for nine months 2026 compares with USD 71.492 million a year earlier, Documentary Fact [CP-1A, company and operating model]. Unmeasured items: ratings, covenant levels and committed liquidity are Insufficient Information, and their absence is not an adverse conclusion.

Thesis. The credit rests on a profitable servicing and origination core and demonstrated access to secured and unsecured funding, set against a large, short-dated and partly uncommitted funding stack that leaves the senior unsecured noteholders exposed to refinancing and structural subordination.

| Governance | Neutral on documented actions; ownership and legal capacity not assessed | Analyst Interpretation; Insufficient Information for ownership | CP-1A governance table |
| Overall | Neutral to cautious, medium confidence | Analyst Interpretation | All of the above |
### Key credit risks

| Refinancing and margin calls on secured lines | Short-dated warehouse and repurchase lines roll against collateral values and advance rates; margin exposure on USD 14.2 billion of secured financing agreements | Forced asset sales or cash drain in a market shock; default risk centred on funding access | Critical |
| Uncommitted capacity | Available financing of USD 10,785.284 million is uncommitted | Headroom may disappear when needed; true liquidity unknown | Material |

| Rate-sensitive earnings | MSR fair value, prepayments and origination margins move with rates; tax charge appears largely non-cash | Cover of funding costs volatile; cash earnings not isolated | Material |

| Structural subordination of senior notes | Unsecured, no subsidiary guarantees, large secured and non-recourse debt | Lower residual value for noteholders; recovery prospects depend on assets left after other claims, no outcome concluded | Material |

| New segments and acquisitions | Fixed costs, depreciation and property debt before earnings scale; Asset Management and Commercial Real Estate lost money before tax | Drag on group earnings and on cash available for debt service | Material |
| Unmeasured covenant and legal terms | Indentures, facility agreements and Total Unencumbered Assets not supplied | Headroom and permissions unknown | Material |
| No credit ratings in the pack | No external view of default risk | Market perception cannot be gauged | Minor |
## Calculations
Inputs are copied from CP-1 and CP-1A; US$ thousands unless stated (1,000 thousand equals USD 1 million).

2. Cash cover of the nearest recourse maturity: 1,708,750 / 6,230,073 = 0.2743 (27.43%). Cash cover of the recourse maturities through 2027: 1,708,750 / 12,967,028 = 0.1318 (13.18%). These are cash balances against contractual maturities, not a liquidity headroom measure, because committed capacity is not supplied and many maturing secured lines are rolled in the ordinary course.
4. Effective tax rate, Q3 2026: 257,819 / 519,093 = 0.4967 (49.67%); nine months 2026: 321,554 / 760,219 = 0.4230 (42.30%). Cash taxes paid for nine months 2026 were 11,398 (CP-1 financials table).

5. Direction of earnings: nine-month net income 438,665 against 627,514 is a change of (438,665 - 627,514) / 627,514 = -0.3009 (a fall of 30.09%); net income attributable to common stockholders 305,150 against 514,084 is a fall of 40.64%.

| Limitation: management claims in the Q3 release are unverified (CP-1A) | Not relied on for figures | Strengths | Minor | None |
Confidence is Medium rather than High because of the material gaps above; no upstream module was blocked.
